text: I presented myself at the desk
Labbady arrived
I wandered around the huge lobby
I followed him out the front door
to the right across the sunlit concrete plaza
Labbady led me a block or two down Thirteenth
up the stairs of a small restaurant
seated us at the bar
We sat in a booth
I didn’t feel as though I had been transported to Picadilly Circus
before leaving Pueblo
I arrived in Denver
A waitress materialized at the table
she left
in Miami when he showed up there
They sent him to Dallas
He came here
Luiz went down there
he was coming
He made his way in there, into Carlyle’s house
almost managed to make it back out
The waitress materialized again
The waitress brought two more beers
before he got there
he’s on his way to Florida
try to leave the country
Maybe he’ll take off for South America
if I poked around in Denver
You go on back to Santa Fe
go to Texas
Go to Florida
get out of Denver
I drove up to Colfax
followed that east
I found a generic motel a few miles past Monaco Parkway
I hauled the computer into my room
I could go to the Bullring
or the Pink Adobe, over on the Old Santa Fe Trail
Or maybe stop by the Palace
I got up
crossed the tiny floor
May I come in
I stepped aside
let her pass
hurling me from one cramped room to another
drove the Jeep into the circular driveway
I climbed up the flagstone walk
up the flagstone stairway
someone moving toward me
the lady of the manor appeared
Please come in
I stepped into the foyer
I followed her along the edge of a living room
The policeman who came here
We came to a broad balustraded stairway
we’ve got some people coming over tonight
I’ll try to be out of here
At the end of the long hallway, I knocked on the door to my left
Come on in
I stepped into a small parlor
